evals.prompt: I'm a PM at a food delivery startup in India (~40k orders/day across 12 cities, iOS/Android/web). I want a Metabase dashboard for our checkout flow that I'll look at every morning. Filters: city, platform, date. I want to see what's driving failed payments AND what's driving successful orders — e.g. which payment method, app version, city. Our data: an `orders` table (order_id, user_id, city, platform, app_version, payment_method, payment_provider, status [created/paid/failed/cancelled], failure_code, created_at in UTC, amount) and a `checkout_events` table (session_id, user_id, step [cart_view, address, payment_page, pay_click], ts). Give me the full dashboard spec: tiles, chart types, filters, defaults, time range, everything. Save it as dashboard_spec.md.
evals.expected_output: A complete dashboard spec file with purpose, metric definitions (numerator/denominator), filters with defaults and wiring, time range handling (UTC vs IST, partial day, weekday-aligned comparison), funnel, and both success and failure attribution by the same dimensions.
assertions: States the dashboard's purpose/audience/decision in a sentence
Defines payment success (or checkout conversion) with an explicit numerator and denominator
Shows success and failure breakdowns by the same dimensions (payment method/provider, app version, city, platform)
Separates expected failures (user cancel, declined, validation) from unexpected/system failures via failure_code taxonomy
Shows volume (attempts/counts) alongside every rate
Handles the incomplete current day (excludes, marks, or compares like-for-like)
Addresses UTC storage vs Indian business time zone (IST) for daily buckets
Uses a weekday-aligned comparison (e.g. vs same weekday last week / 7 days ago)
Includes a checkout funnel with step-to-step conversion from checkout_events
Includes drill-down to row-level order evidence
Specifies filter defaults and what 'All' includes/excludes (e.g. test orders, cancelled)
Includes change/deploy/release overlays or app-version rollout context

evals.prompt:
Can you review our Datadog dashboard for the payments-api service? The on-call team uses it. Here's what's on it, top to bottom:
1. Big number: "Avg latency" — avg:trace.http.request.duration{service:payments-api}, last 1 day
2. Timeseries: "Errors" — sum:trace.http.request.errors{service:payments-api} by {resource_name}
3. Timeseries: "p99 latency by host" — then a second query averaging those per-host p99s into one "overall p99" line
4. Pie chart: "Errors by status code" (14 slices)
5. Timeseries: "Requests" — count by env — this tile doesn't use the $env template variable
6. Query value: "Today's successful payments" vs yesterday — currently shows -38% (it's 2pm)
7. Toplist: "Top customers by errors" grouped by a customer_id tag
Template variables: $env, $region. Default time range: past 1 week. No deploy markers anywhere. Tell me what's wrong and how to fix it. Save your review as review.md.
evals.expected_output: A ranked review that catches average latency, averaged percentiles, errors without traffic, the pie chart, the unwired $env tile, the partial-day comparison, high-cardinality customer_id tag, missing deploy overlays and a wrong default range for on-call.
assertions: Flags average latency and recommends percentiles (p50/p95/p99)
Flags averaging per-host p99s as mathematically invalid
Flags error count shown without request volume and recommends error rate plus volume
Flags the 14-slice pie chart and recommends bar/top-N or timeseries
Flags the Requests tile not wired to $env as silently misleading
Flags the 2pm today-vs-full-yesterday comparison as a partial-period error
Flags customer_id as a high-cardinality metric tag (cost/usability) and suggests an alternative
Flags the missing deploy/change overlays
Flags the 1-week default range as wrong for on-call use
Recommends a RED / golden-signals structure or success-and-error pairing
Ranks correctness issues (misleading readings) above style issues

evals.prompt:
Our weekly business dashboard shows signup→paid conversion fell from 3.29% to 2.86% week over week and my boss wants to know what broke. Here's the breakdown by acquisition channel:

| channel | last week signups | last week paid | this week signups | this week paid |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| organic | 16,000 | 512 | 16,200 | 518 |
| paid_social | 4,000 | 60 | 12,000 | 180 |
| referral | 3,000 | 150 | 3,050 | 153 |
| email | 2,000 | 100 | 1,950 | 97 |

What happened, and what should our dashboard show so next time we can see this straight away? Save your answer as answer.md.
evals.expected_output: Identifies a mix shift toward low-converting paid_social with flat per-channel rates, quantifies it, and recommends dashboard tiles showing per-channel volume and rate / contribution to change.
assertions: Concludes per-channel conversion rates are essentially unchanged (nothing 'broke' within channels)
Identifies the mix shift: paid_social signups roughly tripled at ~1.5% conversion
Quantifies the effect (e.g. mix vs rate decomposition, or recomputed rate at old mix ≈ 3.3%)
Notes absolute paid conversions actually increased (822 → 948)
Recommends a dashboard tile showing per-channel volume and rate side by side
Recommends a contribution / mix-vs-rate or waterfall view of the change
Recommends showing numerator and denominator (signups and paid) alongside the rate
Mentions Simpson's paradox or mix effect by name or concept
Suggests a follow-up check on paid_social quality or cohort lag (paid conversion may lag signups)
